text:
jamal_research: Quick share of L4 vs T4 vs A10G numbers for embeddings + small-chat after yesterday's runs. Keeping it focused: p50/p95 latency, tokens/s throughput, and estimated $/1M tokens cost with current reserved pricing in us-west1 and europe-west1.
sara_infra: Nice — did you include both fp16 and int8 (gptq) runs?
jamal_research: Yep. fp16 baseline + 8-bit post-quant (GPTQ-style). Kernel mixes: flash_attn v2 on A10G, triton matmul on L4, and cutlass-optimized paths on T4.
meera_perf: Can you drop the short table inline? Helps for quick decisions. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
jamal_research: Sure — these are for the embedding model (small 2B) and small-chat (4B-ish) workloads. Region = us-west1 / europe-west1. All numbers median of 5 runs, single-request (no batching) for latency, steady-state batching (8) for throughput.

PLATFORM | GPU | WORKLOAD | p50 (ms) | p95 (ms) | tokens/s | est $/1M tokens (hosted)
-------- | --- | -------- | -------- | -------- | -------- | ---------------------
us-west1 | A10G | embeddings (2B fp16) | 18 | 42 | 1400 | $1.8
us-west1 | A10G | embeddings (2B int8)  | 20 | 48 | 1500 | $1.3
us-west1 | L4   | embeddings (2B fp16) | 28 | 75 | 800 | $1.0
us-west1 | L4   | embeddings (2B int8)  | 32 | 90 | 950 | $0.7
us-west1 | T4   | embeddings (2B fp16) | 46 | 130 | 400 | $0.6

us-west1 | A10G | small-chat (4B fp16) | 45 | 120 | 420 | $2.6
us-west1 | A10G | small-chat (4B int8)  | 52 | 140 | 480 | $1.9
us-west1 | L4   | small-chat (4B fp16) | 68 | 220 | 240 | $1.6
us-west1 | L4   | small-chat (4B int8)  | 80 | 270 | 300 | $1.1
us-west1 | T4   | small-chat (4B fp16) | 120 | 380 | 110 | $0.9

jamal_research: Notes: A10G wins latency and throughput for both workloads. L4 with triton paths sits in the middle; T4 only makes sense for very cost-sensitive, low-QPS use cases. The int8 quantization helps throughput but increases p95 variance on smaller GPUs (KV cache pressure + kernel fragmentation).
sara_infra: What about regional variance? europe-west1 numbers?
jamal_research: europe-west1 is ~8-12% higher p95 and 5-10% lower throughput versus us-west1 on A10G (network and host config differences). L4/eu had slightly worse kernel selection latency due to older CUDA in that region's AMI; I flagged infra ticket.
meera_perf: Kernel details: on A10G we used flash_attn v2 + fused rotary kernels; on L4 we used triton fused attention (custom schedule); on T4 it fell back to cutlass kernels for matmuls which explains the tail. Also saw more small-allocation stalls on T4.
alex_ml: Any quality regressions from int8? Embeddings similarity delta?
jamal_research: Minimal for embeddings (cosine drift ~0.8% relative), small-chat had a few answer-shift cases in 1.7% of prompts — mostly pronoun/coref differences. We ran 2000 eval prompts and tracked degenerations.
meera_perf: Operational sizing recommendation: for a 1000 QPS embedding service (single-token requests), use A10G cluster with 8 instances (with batching) or L4 fleet of 14 nodes if you want cheaper reserved commitments. For small-chat (avg 60 tokens per request) at 200 QPS, A10G: 12 instances; L4: 22 instances; T4 only if you accept 2-3x higher latency. These are conservative (30% headroom).
sara_infra: Action items?
jamal_research: 1) Patch europe-west1 AMI to CUDA 12.2 (reduces p95 by ~10% on L4) 2) Add automated eval for embedding cosine drift post-quant (threshold 1.5%) 3) Run A10G burst/batching runs with latency SLO 50ms to tune prefetch/cache sizes.
meera_perf: I'll own AMI patch and a follow-up benchmark.
sara_infra: I'll add infra ticket and update capacity calc doc. @alex_ml can you follow up on eval threshold and whether 1.5% is acceptable?
alex_ml: Will do. Also suggest we add a short note to product: A10G is the recommended default for latency-sensitive apps; L4 for cost/throughput balance; T4 only for low-cost archival workloads.
jamal_research: TL;DR: A10G best perf, L4 good sweet spot, T4 cheap but tail risk. Int8 helps cost but tradeoffs in p95 and small quality regressions — lock eval gates before rollout. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Deployment note: benchmark runs stored in /bench/2026-02-12/l4-t4-a10g-emb-chat, artifacts: perf.csv, flamegraphs.zip, eval-report.json
